availability.comment: Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered. Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports. London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.

Zaccheaus caught two of his four targets for 17 yards and returned five punts for 81 yards during Atlanta's loss Sunday versus the Chiefs. Zaccheaus recorded a season-high 17 receiving yards during the loss while playing 29 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.

Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Cousins completed 26 of 38 passes for 235 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for no gain. After throwing a pick-six among his three interceptions when he faced San Francisco's defense in his final game with the Raiders in Week 9, Cousins had another interception returned for a touchdown by the 49ers in the second quarter of Sunday's loss. The Vikings took a 28-10 deficit into the halftime locker room, and Cousins was unable to orchestrate a comeback before Minnesota waved the white flag and inserted Carson Wentz for its final drive. Cousins is still strengthening his grasp on the offense two games into his reunion with the Vikings ahead of a Week 12 visit from the Falcons, with whom Cousins spent the previous two seasons.

Jones rushed eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown while catching his lone target for 13 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. Jones tied the game with an 11-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, but the 49ers outscored the Vikings 21-3 in the second quarter, forcing Minnesota into a more pass-heavy approach. Jordan Mason led the team with 38 rushing yards on 11 carries. Jones and Mason should continue to split carries in Week 12 against the Falcons, with Jones offering greater upside as a pass catcher.

Mason rushed 11 times for 38 yards while catching his lone target for minus-1 yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. Mason had one more carry and eight more rushing yards than Aaron Jones, but Jones' totals included an 11-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. They have worked in a near-even split when both veteran RBs have been healthy, but Mason hasn't scored since Week 1. Between his lack of TDs and minimal involvement as a pass catcher (three receptions for six yards in six games), Mason hasn't provided much fantasy value ahead of a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.

Jennings caught three of six targets for 20 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. Jennings made his return to action after missing two games with a calf injury. The 29-year-old reeled in a season-high three passes, while his six targets were also the most he's had in a game this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 40 receiving yards in contest, and Jennings hasn't scored a touchdown this season. His next chance to accomplish both feats will come in Week 12 versus the Falcons.

Jefferson caught seven of nine targets for 86 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. Jefferson has experienced an uptick in usage since the Vikings reacquired Kirk Cousins. The star WR has 16 catches for 160 yards on 22 targets in two games with Cousins, though Jefferson hasn't scored since Week 8. Jefferson fumbled at the end of a 25-yard catch in the third quarter, turning what would have been one of his best plays of the night into a lowlight. Another heavy dose of targets from Cousins likely awaits Jefferson in Week 12 against the Falcons.

Felton is poised to maintain an expanded role Sunday against the Falcons, as Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports that Jordan Addison (thumb) will remain sidelined. Felton stepped up in Addison's absence during the Week 11 loss to San Francisco, leading the Vikings with 12 targets en route to six catches for 42 yards. Jauan Jennings and Myles Price also are candidates for additional targets from Kirk Cousins behind Justin Jefferson against a Falcons defense that gives up the fifth-most passing yards per game.

Hockenson (wrist) caught six of seven targets for 55 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. In his return from a one-game absence, Hockenson finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Justin Jefferson's 86. Hockenson showed promising chemistry with Kirk Cousins after the veteran TE sat out Cousins' return to Minnesota during the Week 10 win over Green Bay. Cousins was under center for the Vikings in the 2023 regular season, when Hockenson set career highs with 95 catches for 960 yards. Hockenson hasn't surpassed 455 yards in a regular season since, though he's on pace to do so this year, with 41 catches for 383 yards and three touchdowns through nine appearances heading into a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.

Brissett completed 24 of 37 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers. He added seven rushing yards on two carries. It was another decent showing for the veteran quarterback, and his first TD pass in two games as a Raven came on a trick that involved a direct snap to Derrick Henry, who flipped it Brissett for a 52-yard strike to Rashod Bateman. Brissett has also kept Zay Flowers relevant, feeding the wideout 18 targets for a 14-171-0 line. Baltimore's passing attack will try to keep improving in Week 12 against the Texans.

Henry (concussion) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans, per Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio. Henry has cleared concussion protocol after practicing without limitations Thursday and Friday. He'll try to help the Ravens snap a six-game losing streak Sunday against the Texans. Running room could be hard to come by against a stout Houston front that's allowing fewer than 100 rushing yards per game, though Henry has overcome more than his fair share of daunting matchups over the years.

Hill carried the ball six times for 69 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers. Derrick Henry had a strong performance as well but was knocked out of the game in the fourth quarter and got checked for a concussion. Hill was heavily involved in the offense prior to that, however, scoring from 19 yards out in the late in the second quarter. He almost had a second TD earlier in the quarter, but Hill had the ball punched loose at the one-yard line after a 36-yard scamper and saw it bounce out of the end zone for a turnover and a touchback. Henry cleared the concussion protocol after the game and figures to be active in the Week 12 against the Texans, but Hill's usage appears to be on the upswing as the Ravens' No. 2 back.

Lane didn't garner a target during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers. Lane failed to reel in a pass for the second time in three weeks, and both times the ball was thrown his way Sunday, the play was negated by a defensive penalty, resulting in no targets for the rookie. He was on the field for 33 offensive snaps, ranking third at wide receiver for Baltimore behind Rashod Bateman (59) and Zay Flowers (57). Lane's next chance to get back on track will come in Week 12 against the Texans.

Bateman (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports. Bateman was limited in Wednesday's session due to a groin injury, but his full practice Thursday puts the sixth-year wide receiver on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. He hauled in his second touchdown of the year in a Week 11 loss to the Panthers and is up to a 25-403-2 receiving line on 42 targets through 11 regular-season games.

Flowers (ankle) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice. Flowers was limited at practice Wednesday, but the wide receiver's quick return to all activity one day later clears the way for him to suit up Sunday against the Texans. In his last outing, Flowers (who has recorded a fantasy-friendly 57-785-3 line on 82 targets through 10 games), was on the field for 88 percent of his team's snaps on offense in a 35-33 loss to the Panthers in Week 11 en route to catching eight of his game-high 11 targets for 97 yards.

Andrews caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to Carolina. While the veteran tight end showed some instant chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett last week, Andrews saw his target volume crater in their second game together, as rookie depth TEs Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner saw similar usage as pass catchers. Andrews has failed to reach 25 receiving yards in five of his last six games and hasn't scored a TD in seven straight contests, making him a very risky fantasy option in Week 12 against the Texans.

Stroud completed 21 of 26 passes for 194 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed six times for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Stroud's night got off to a rocky start when a deflected pass resulted in an interception on the Texans' opening drive, but the red-hot signal-caller was near perfect from that point forward. The 2023 first-round pick went on to toss three touchdown passes for the second straight game and multiple scores for the fifth consecutive contest overall. Stroud connected with Nico Collins (42 yards), Kayshon Boutte (24 yards) and Marlin Klein (13 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, and he'll take a sparkling 22:4 TD:INT into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Montgomery operated as the Texans' RB1 against the Colts in Week 11, but he could see a dip in touches due to the impending return of Woody Marks (concussion) for Sunday's game against the Ravens. Marks was in the league's concussion protocol for Week 11, when Montgomery led the Texans backfield with 26 carries for 107 yards and three catches (on four targets) for 17 yards in a 26-3 win over the Colts. Marks' return means the second-year pro and Montgomery will share the field Sunday for the first time since Week 5 against the Titans, when the latter suffered a groin injury that caused him to miss the Texans' next four games. The duo should split work Sunday against a Baltimore defense that has given up at least 146 rushing yards in three of the team's last four games (all losses).

Marks (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens. Marks, who was inactive Nov. 19 against the Colts, logged 'full' listings at practice Wednesday through Friday and now has gained clearance to rejoin the lineup after being sidelined for one game. His Week 11 absence coincided with the return to action of fellow RB David Montgomery, and now that both backs are available for the first time since Week 5, look for Marks to see a noticeable dip in volume while sharing touches with Montgomery, who logged 26 carries versus Indianapolis.

Harrison (hamstring) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. Harrison has missed the Texans' last two contests, but after a limited practice Wednesday, the wideout's full participation Thursday sets the stage for him to return to action Sunday against the Ravens. Given Harrison's modest production over three outings since arriving in a trade with the Cardinals, he profiles as a speculative fantasy lineup option in Week 12, with Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and possibly Kayshon Boutte (hip, 'DNP' Thursday) also in Houston's WR mix.

Collins secured three of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Facing a Colts defense down both Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee), Collins looked primed for a big night early when he recorded a 42-yard touchdown grab to cap off Houston's second possession. However, C.J. Stroud proceeded to spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, leading to Collins tying his second-lowest reception tally and posting his third-lowest yardage total of the season. However, the star wideout did extend his touchdown streak to three games, and he'll next take aim at what has been an inconsistent Ravens secondary in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Dell secured three of four targets for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. The speedy wideout finished tied for second in receptions for the Texans on a night when C.J. Stroud recorded completions to nine different targets overall. Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Hutchinson caught two of three targets for 13 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts. Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new career highs across the board.

Schultz (illness) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens. Schultz practiced without limitations Friday, shedding any doubts about his availability after an illness limited his participation Thursday. The Ravens have allowed seven TDs to TEs this season, which is seventh most in the NFL, but Schultz has scored only once all season and is coming off consecutive one-catch performances.

Burrow completed 28 of 40 passes for 300 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed twice for minus-1 yard in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night. The Bengals offense started slowly and was shut out altogether in the first quarter, but Burrow was able to lead his team to 10 second-quarter points partly via a 31-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins. The prolific signal-caller added a four-yard scoring toss to Colbie Young in the third quarter, and Burrow then helped lead Cincinnati downfield for a go-ahead Evan McPherson 56-yard field goal with 46 seconds remaining, albeit after narrowly avoiding an interception and then taking a third-down sack. Nevertheless, the Bengals came up short when Jayden Daniels led the Commanders on a five-play, 64-yard game-winning march, but Burrow finished with his fourth tally of at least 300 passing yards this season. He'll look to put his team back in the win column in a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.

Brown rushed six times for six yards and brought in five of eight targets for 30 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night. As his final line indicates, Brown was completely stonewalled by a talented Commanders run defense, although backfield mate Samaje Perine, who equaled Brown's carry total, was able to average 4.3 yards per tote with his opportunities and  added 71 receiving yards. Brown did find a way to make his usual impact as a receiver, tying for the team lead in receptions and finishing second in targets to Ja'Marr Chase. Brown's carry and rushing yardage totals were both season lows, but he should have appreciably better conditions for production on the ground in a Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.

Perine turned six carries into 26 yards and caught all four of his targets for 71 yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday. The Commanders' defense focused its attention toward slowing down both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. That opened up the field for Perine, with most of his production coming on a 44-yard catch late in the second quarter, and the drive ended two plays later with a 31-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Higgins. Perine finished second on the Bengals in both catches and receiving yards behind tight end Mike Gesicki, and the RB's 26 rushing yards were well ahead of Chase Brown's six. Perine has at least 10 touches in each of his last three games, but Cincinnati's offense is mustering only 79.4 rushing yards per game, which is third-worst in the NFL. Given Brown's struggles this season, Perine could take on a larger role in the backfield for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

Meyers caught one of two passes for two yards, returned six kickoffs for 150 yards and returned one punt for five yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday. Most of Meyers' production came on special teams as a returner, and his one catch was his fewest since Week 7 against the Ravens, when he failed to record a reception. He's caught two passes or fewer in seven of 10 regular-season games, and his minimal role on offense would shrink even more once Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is cleared to return from injured reserve. The Bengals will head home for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

Chase secured five of nine targets for 31 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night. The Commanders focused on keeping Chase in check after his 231-yard outburst against the Steelers in Week 10, and they executed that plan to near perfection. The superstar wideout finished with his third-lowest yardage total of the season, and his sparsest since Week 4. Chase still extended his streak of five-plus-catch efforts to six games, and he'll look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 12 home matchup against a vulnerable Saints defense Sunday.

After not practicing Friday, Higgins (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports. Higgins wasn't on the Bengals' Week 12 injury report until Friday, but after missing the team's final practice, the wideout's status is now worth tracking ahead of Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. While a late-week downgrade in practice participation like this can't be ignored, Ben Baby of ESPN.com notes that "Higgins just woke up with some soreness" Friday and that the team gave the WR "the day to work through it." More importantly, Baby indicates that the issue isn't a concern in terms of Higgins' availability versus New Orleans.

Gesicki brought in five of six targets for 77 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night. The veteran tight end finished with a team-high yardage total while coming just a yard short of equaling his best tally of the season as well. Gesicki's biggest catch came late in the fourth quarter on the Bengals' final drive, when he hauled in a 32-yard pass from Joe Burrow over the middle to get the Bengals down to  the Commanders' 33-yard line. Gesicki's production continues to have some game-to-game volatility, but he'll draw another favorable matchup in a Week 12 home clash with the Saints on Sunday.

Shough completed 25 of 42 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears. He added 34 rushing yards on three carries. Despite the high volume of attempts, Shough couldn't get much going through the air while dealing with a ferocious Chicago pass rush that sacked him six times, including one for a fourth-quarter safety by Montez Sweat. Shough has gone four straight games without producing multiple TDs, posting a 4:3 TD:INT over that stretch while completing 67.3 percent of his passes with a weak 6.3 YPA. The second-year QB will likely need to be a lot more productive in Week 12 if the Saints are going to keep up with Joe Burrow and the Bengals.

Kamara rushed one time for one yard and caught a one-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears. The veteran running back played just eight of 72 offensive snaps, while both CJ Donaldson and Travis Etienne played 32 each with Audric Estime a healthy inactive. Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. The Saints' three-man backfield continues to be one to try and avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions. Kamara's proverbial gas tank is nearing empty, but the Saints continue to give him high-value touches near the goal line while refusing to play him outside of the red zone.

Estime (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bears. Estime's role in the offense was reduced in Week 10 against the Panthers, which marked Travis Etienne's return from a five-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Estime is a healthy scratch for Sunday's game, which means Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson will operate as the rotational options out of the backfield behind Etienne. Estime's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

Etienne carried the ball 14 times for 76 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 21-13 loss to Chicago. The former Jaguar was the clear No. 1 option in the backfield for the Saints. Alvin Kamara saw just two touches and CJ Donaldson handled five, although Kamara did vulture another red-zone TD on a one-yard reception in the second quarter, Most of Etienne's production came on a 46-yard scamper that saw him tackled just short of the goal line, setting up Kamara's score, but the fact that he was able to produce his first big play as a Saint was still encouraging. Etienne will attempt to build on this performance in Week 12 against the Bengals.

Olave caught nine of 15 targets for 102 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears. One week after taking a back seat to rookie Jordyn Tyson, Olave re-emerged as Tyler Shough's favorite downfield option, as he set a new season high in targets and topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time in 2026. Tyson, meanwhile, caught only one pass on two targets, suggesting the Saints' aerial attack may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game. Olave will look to make an impact again in Week 12 against the Bengals.

Vele caught seven passes for 76 yards on seven targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears. Vele continues to run virtually every route for New Orleans, and the seven grabs matched his season high from Week 1 against the Lions, while Vele's 76 yards are a new high-water mark for the receiver. It was notable that Jordyn Tyson ran just 22 routes on Tyler Shough's 51 dropbacks against Chicago. The Saints offense has become tough to predict on a week-to-week basis. Vele is more of a low-ceiling fantasy WR4/5 most weeks.

Tyson caught one of two targets for six yards and added four rushing yards on his only carry in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears. One week after logging 13 targets as Tyler Shough's top downfield option, Tyson all but disappeared as Chris Olave instead saw WR1-worthy volume. The Saints' aerial attack simply may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game, which would mark Tyson as a volatile, but high-ceiling, fantasy asset for the rest of the season. The rookie will try to bounce back in Week 12 against the Bengals.

Fant (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals, while Juwan Johnson (hamstring) has been ruled out, Matthew Paras of the New Orleans Times-Picayune reports. Fant would be in line to operate as the top TE for the Saints if he gets the green light to suit up against the team for which he played last season. The 29-year-old Fant has scored either three or four touchdowns in six of his eight NFL regular seasons, including three apiece in 2025 with Cincinnati and so far in 2026 with New Orleans. Rookie third-round pick Oscar Delp is the next tight end up if Fant joins Johnson on the sidelines.

Taylor will be joined in the backfield in Sunday's game against the Giants by Anthony Richardson, who was named the Colts' new starting quarterback after Daniel Jones was cut Friday, Mike Chappell of Fox 59 News Indianapolis reports. Taylor is slated to take his first extended snaps alongside Richardson since the 2024 season, when the two started together 10 times. The threat that Richardson presented to defenses as a runner seemed to aid Taylor's own effectiveness, as the running back averaged 4.8 yards per carry and scored eight touchdowns over that 10-game stretch. Now two years later, the Colts have a much less formidable offensive line in place and few established pass-catching weapons that defenses need to hone in on, so Taylor will likely be hard-pressed to match the lofty production he previously achieved with Richardson under center. Additionally, the 3-8 Colts may be cognizant of not overworking Taylor amid a losing season, though the loss of top backup Seth McGowan (hamstring) for at least Week 12 may result in Taylor seeing a slight uptick in opportunities after he played fewer than 70 percent of snaps in each of the last five games and averaged 16.6 touches in those contests.

Dulin caught two of his four targets for 30 yards and assisted on two tackles on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night. Dulin played 22 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver saw plenty of attention, catching 50 percent of his targets to accumulate the second-highest receiving yardage for the Colts, behind Anthony Gould's 48 yards.

Burks was targeted three times for zero catches, had one kick return for 10 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night. Burks was the No. 2 wide receiver for the Colts in the contest. Despite being targeted three times, the wide receiver could not haul in any passes from since-cut quarterback Daniel Jones. Burks played 32 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps in the contest.

McCarthy completed 18 of 38 passes for 173 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions and rushed seven times for 33 yards in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. McCarthy had his share of trouble against an aggressive Jaguars defense, leading to a season-worst 47.4 percent completion rate. However, the emerging signal-caller avoided turnovers and connected with Malik Nabers for an eight-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter. McCarthy also provided some timely contributions with his legs, and he's averaging 5.4 yards on his 22 rush attempts to date. McCarthy connected with nine different targets overall as he continues to show good command of the offense, and he'll look to bounce back efficiency-wise in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

Skattebo rushed 14 times for 34 yards and brought in three of seven targets for 14 yards in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Skattebo was unsurprisingly stymied on the ground by the Jaguars' elite run defense, and he couldn't really make up for it with his work through the air. Skattebo also committed another untimely turnover, fumbling at Jacksonville's 31-yard line with just over four minutes remaining in the third quarter and New York trying to add to a 20-6 lead. The change of possession ultimately didn't lead to any Jaguars points, however, and head coach John Harbaugh showed some faith in the second-year back by affording him the opportunity to ice the upset win with three carries on the final drive. Skattebo proved up to the task by netting 13 yards on those touches to force the Jags to exhaust their timeouts, and he should continue helming the backfield in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

Singletary finished with one carry for five yards and one catch for five yards in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars. The running back played just 10 offensive snaps behind starter Cam Skattebo. Singletary has averaged just 2.9 yards per carry this year on 41 attempts.

Mooney did not catch any of his five targets during Sunday's 23-18 win versus the Jaguars. Quarterback J.J. McCarthy was inefficient against a solid Jaguars defense in Week 11, completing just 18 of his 38 pass attempts for 173 yards. A couple of those 20 incompletions were intended for an open Mooney, who continued to operate in the deeper areas of the field. He'll keep hunting for a big play in Week 12 at Indianapolis.

Fields caught two of his five targets for 25 yards in the Giants' 23-15 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Fields played 56 offensive snaps in the contest, logging 86 percent of the Giants' such plays. Despite the lack of catches, the No. 2 wide receiver continues to receive attention from quarterback J.J. McCarthy on a week-to-week basis.

Nabers brought in seven of 12 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Nabers was in the familiar position of leading the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and the third-year star also snapped a four-game touchdown drought with an eight-yard grab in the second quarter. Nabers has at least five catches in eight straight contests and three double-digit target tallies within that span, and the 2024 first-round pick should continue to be the subject of plenty of J.J. McCarthy's attention in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

Likely (groin) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at Indianapolis, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Likely was listed as limited on the injury report Wednesday and Thursday due to the groin strain that he picked up in practice last Friday, but it won't keep him from suiting up again in Week 12. While playing through the issue this past Sunday against the Jaguars, he took on a normal 76 percent snap share but recorded just one catch (on three targets) for 35 yards.

availability.comment: Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. He also rushed once for four yards. Smith didn't have a completion longer than 21 yards but kept the offense on schedule with an accurate performance. Most importantly, he stepped up in the red zone, which has been the team's Achilles' heel throughout the season. Smith threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to Breece Hall to snap the Jets' two-game touchdown drought in the second quarter, then tacked on touchdown passes of eight and 15 yards to practice-squad elevation Sterling Shepard. The veteran QB will take a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 12 road game against the Dolphins, who defeated the Jets in Week 7 despite three touchdown passes from Smith.

Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards while catching his lone target for nine yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. Allen's 16 carries matched his total from the previous two games combined, as he had seen a downtick in opportunities since fellow RB Breece Hall returned from a quadriceps injury. Hall led the backfield once again with 100 scrimmage yards and a touchdown on 23 touches, but Allen was a key part of the game plan as well in the run-heavy win. The Jets will face a one-win team for a second consecutive game in Week 12 at Miami, which could allow Allen to stay involved alongside Hall.

Mitchell caught two passes for 30 yards on three targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. Even with Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) inactive, Mitchell's role didn't change, as his three targets tied with two other teammates for second on the team behind Garrett Wilson's five on a day the Jets called 37 run plays to just 22 passes. Mitchell has just one touchdown this season and has only 14 catches for 212 yards and no touchdowns in six games surrounding his 7-142-1 receiving performance from Week 8 against the Raiders. He's a big-play specialist in an offense that prefers to feed Wilson and its running backs.

Sadiq caught all three of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. Sadiq finished tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and running back Breece Hall behind wideout Garrett Wilson (five). The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for just the second time since catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a score in Week 3 against the Lions. Sadiq has now caught 25 of 36 targets for 268 yards and a score while adding a three-yard rushing touchdown over the first 11 regular-season contests of his career.

Taylor caught two passes for 25 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. The Jets controlled this game from start to finish and never trailed, so Geno Smith attempted just 21 passes to 37 run plays for New York. Taylor's 25 yards were his most in a game since Week 7, and he's totaled just 10 catches for 75 yards and no touchdowns over his last four contests. He's a very risky play as a fantasy tight end.

With Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) ruled out, Rodriguez is slated to operate as the Jaguars' top backfield option for Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports. Tuten was held out of practice all week due to a left ankle/foot injury that he aggravated during the Jaguars' Week 11 loss to the Giants. That means Rodriguez will take on the RB1 role for Sunday's game against a Titans defense that has given up at least 40 points in three consecutive games and ranks 25th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (127.1). Rodriguez has logged 63 carries for 261 yards (4.1 YPC) and four touchdowns and caught five of six targets for 49 yards across 10 regular-season games in 2026.

Thomas could handle a larger role Sunday against the Titans, as Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports that Parker Washington (shoulder) won't suit up. Thomas has had a disappointing third season in Jacksonville, mustering a meager 84 receiving yards over his last eight appearances while seemingly having fallen out of favor in coach Liam Coen's offense. Washington's absence against Tennessee's struggling secondary could provide Thomas with an opportunity to turn back the clock and put up a performance reminiscent of the 2024 first-round pick's elite rookie season. Jakobi Meyers and Josh Cameron also are in line for expanded roles in Jacksonville's wide-receiver room.

Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports. Meyers has managed to shake off an ankle injury that limited his practice participation earlier in the week. He racked up a season-high 85 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 11 loss to the Giants, and Meyers is likely to get plenty of attention from Trevor Lawrence against Tennessee's league-worst secondary Sunday in the absence of top Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (shoulder), giving Meyers appealing upside in nearly all fantasy formats.

Cameron is in line to handle a larger role Sunday against the Titans, as Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports that Parker Washington (shoulder) won't suit up. Cameron and Brian Thomas are the top candidates to absorb extra targets alongside Jakobi Meyers in Washington's absence. Washington is considered week-to-week, so his absence could extend beyond Week 12. Cameron has 111 receiving yards and a touchdown over the past two games, so the rookie sixth-round pick was trending up even prior to Washington's injury. An increased role against a Titans defense that's giving up the most catches and yards per game to wide receivers could set Cameron up for a breakout performance.

Ward completed 21 of 30 passes for 248 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for three yards and another score in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Ward's final line belies his struggles somewhat, as a Cowboys defense that made a defensive playcaller switch brought him down for five sacks and forced a lost fumble on one of them at Dallas' 20-yard line. Ward did manage to connect with Carnell Tate (59 yards) and Calvin Ridley (12 yards) for his pair of TD passes, the first coming when the rookie wideout alertly got up after not being touched and the second on a broken play where Ward threw across the field after buying several extra seconds with his legs. Ward also had a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, and despite Tennessee's team-level misery, the second-year signal-caller has thrown for at least 231 yards and two touchdowns in three consecutive games heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

Ridley caught five of six targets for 68 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys. Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

Tate brought in two of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. Tate had a fairly non-descript day overall despite the Titans' 30-point output, but he rewarded fantasy managers with a 59-yard catch-and run touchdown in the third quarter on which he alertly got up and ran down the left sideline after Cowboys defenders failed to touch him while he was down. The rookie fourth overall pick was making his return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and the score served as Tate's second of his career, both which have come in his last three games. Tate has at least 58 receiving yards in five of the last six contests, including in three straight, heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

Dike caught six of seven targets for 69 yards during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys. Dike was able to reel in multiple passes for the third straight game, and his six snags set a new season high for the second-year pro. The 24-year-old paced the team in targets Sunday, narrowly edging out fellow wide receivers Calvin Ridley (six) and Carnell Tate (five). Dike will have a chance to continue carving out a more substantial role for himself on offense moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign.

Ayomanor caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Sunday's loss to Dallas. Ayomanor logged season highs with five catches, 10 targets and 79 yards against Jacksonville in Week 10, but he reverted back closer to his usual numbers versus the Cowboys. The second-year wideout did rank third on the team in receptions and receiving yards, and his 37 offensive snaps also were third behind Carnell Tate (62) and Chimere Dike (54). Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season, but Ayomanor may be hard-pressed to put up reliable fantasy production as the third pass-catching option, at best, for one of the league's least prolific air attacks.

Helm caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys. The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and was unable to get anything going against arguably the league's worst defense Sunday. Helm has been held below 30 receiving yards in nine of 10 games this season. He's nothing more than a low-end TE2 in fantasy.

availability.comment: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that DeVito is the team's starting quarterback, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. "We're excited about that. He had a good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said of DeVito. With Drake Maye (fibula) hurt early in Week 10 against Detroit, DeVito stepped in at quarterback but managed to complete just 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He added 19 yards on four carries. The 28-year-old does have some starting experience -- he helmed the Giants offense for eight starts between 2023 and 2024 -- but he didn't play at all in 2025. For now, the Patriots are at least communicating that they'll stand pat and not look for help at quarterback outside the organization. However, the team is barely hanging on in the AFC playoff race with a 5-5 record, and with only rookie Behren Morton on the active roster as a healthy option to DeVito, the team may still look elsewhere if DeVito is unable to show better production.

Stevenson was not listed on the Patriots' practice report Wednesday. Stevenson hurt his knee in Week 9 against Green Bay and initially appeared slated to miss multiple games. However, he surprisingly was able to suit up in Week 10 against Detroit in Munich, Germany, though he logged just a 44 percent offensive snap share and gained only five yards on seven touches. Stevenson is now off the injury report entirely to begin Week 12 prep following New England's Week 11 bye, suggesting that the knee issue is no longer a concern. The veteran running back commented Wednesday on his ability to suit up in Week 10, attributing it to "a bunch of recovery" and sharing, "(The trainers) did a good job of just getting me available again... Leg wasn't feeling 100 percent, but I was well enough to go out there and participate with the team and try to help them out a little bit," per Sophie Weller of Patriots Wire. With no practice restrictions to begin Week 12 prep, Stevenson should be set to suit up this Sunday  in Los Angeles against the Chargers, when he'll be taking handoffs from QB Tommy DeVito.

Douglas is set to maintain a prominent role Sunday against the Chargers, as A.J. Brown (hamstring) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) won't play. Douglas had 178 yards and a touchdown in a career-best two-game stretch spanning Weeks 8 and 9, but he was limited to one catch for four yards in his most recent appearance, which QB Drake Maye (lower leg) left early. With Tommy DeVito under center in Week 12, Douglas will try to get back on track in New England's banged-up passing game coming out of a bye week.

Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10. A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.

Hollins is set to work in a starting role Sunday against the Chargers, as A.J. Brown (hamstring) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) won't play. Hollins led the Patriots with five catches for 48 yards in their 35-10 Week 10 loss to the Lions prior to a Week 11 bye. He showed the best chemistry out of New England's pass catchers with Tommy DeVito, who replaced Drake Maye (lower leg) against Detroit and is expected to start Sunday's game. Hollins has 23 catches for 293 yards and one touchdown in six appearances this season.

Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich. The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of plays, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. Raridon also has been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. He's averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

Darnold (quadriceps) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at San Francisco, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports. Darnold thus is returning from a two-game absence due to a quad injury and cracked ribs, benefiting from the Seahawks' Week 11 bye. When asked if Darnold is 100 percent, head coach Mike Macdonald told Bell that "pretty much nobody is fully health at this point in the season," indicating that the quarterback still may be dealing with residual effects of those health concerns. In any case, Darnold will resume starting duties for the Seahawks this weekend.

Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas. This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas. Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday. It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Smith-Njigba (ankle) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest in San Francisco, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports. The Seahawks listed Smith-Njigba as limited on the first two Week 12 injury reports due to an ankle issue, but he'll play through it in Sunday's NFC West showdown. In the first matchup with the 49ers back in Week 5, he hauled in five of eight targets for 102 yards and one touchdown.

Shaheed caught one pass for eight yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.

Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan announced that Jones will start in place of Brock Purdy (ankle) on Sunday against the Seahawks. Purdy didn't practice this week and was ruled out for Week 12 on Friday, setting Jones up for his first start of the campaign. In eight starts for an injured Purdy in 2025, Jones went 5-3, completed 201 of 289 passes (69.6 percent) for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions, rushed 28 times for 64 yards and fumbled four times (two lost).

Evans (Achilles) is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest against the Seahawks, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports. Evans didn't practice Wednesday before he was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report as he continues to deal with the right Achilles tendinitis that forced him out of a Week 6 matchup with the Commanders. He returned to action this past Sunday versus the Vikings in Mexico City and gathered in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown on a 43 percent snap share. Evans' status will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

availability.comment: Daniels completed 23 of 35 passes for 289 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and added six carries for 55 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night. Daniels looked like he was on his way to a middling night during a first half in which he led the Commanders to just seven points, but the 2024 first-round pick flipped a switch in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter. Daniels led field-goal drives of 13, 11 and five plays that netted a total of 193 yards during the final period, the last one featuring strikes of 22 and 42 yards to Antonio Williams to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning field goal. Daniels finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, and he also mustered his seventh interception-free effort of the campaign. Having helped Washington to a critical victory, he'll look to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown and brought in two of three targets for 23 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night. Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Croskey-Merritt outpaced Austin Ekeler, the only other Commanders back to log a carry, by six rush attempts. The second-year pro also recorded his third rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run with 12 seconds remaining in the first half. Croskey-Merritt averaged over 4.0 yards per carry for the second straight game after failing to eclipse that mark in each of the first four games of the season, and he should be in store for an even busier day in a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

Williams brought in nine of 11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night. The rookie third-round pick managed new career highs across all three components of his receiving line, which also all served as team-best totals Monday. Williams' last two catches of the night were his most critical, as he recorded 22- and 42-yard grabs on Washington's final drive to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning 26-yard field goal. Williams hadn't topped 54 receiving yards in any game after a 64-yard effort in his pro debut in Week 1, but Monday night's breakout could serve as a launchpad to a strong stretch run as the Commanders make a playoff push.

Diggs (personal) was removed from the Commanders' injury report Thursday. Diggs had an excused absence Wednesday but avoided the injury report entirely one day later, setting him up to continue to serve as Washington's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver. Since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season due to a torn patellar tendon that he suffered in Week 6 at San Francisco, Diggs has compiled a 16-217-2 line on 27 targets over the last four games.

Burks (foot) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Arizona. Burks opened Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited listings due to a lingering foot injury, but a full practice Friday has him in the clear ahead of the weekend. In three appearances since Week 8 while playing with the issue, he's combined for a 7-138-0 line on 11 targets during that span.

Okonkwo brought in four of five targets for 66 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night. Okonkwo contributed his game-long 32-yard grab on his first catch of the night, and the veteran tight end went on to finish second in receiving yards for the Commanders. He also contributed a key 13-yard grab on Washington's penultimate drive that culminated in a key field goal, and in all, three of his four receptions resulted in first downs. Okonkwo has at least four catches in three straight games but still is seeking his first touchdown of the season heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while adding eight rushes for 49 yards and a score in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with Cleveland. Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

Sampson rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans. Sampson hardly carries the ball for Cleveland and is merely the pass-catching complement to Quinshon Judkins out of the backfield. Across five games this season, Sampson has rushed 19 times for 79  yards while adding 16 catches for 152 yards on 22 targets. He's playable in PPR fantasy leagues as a desperation RB2 option, particularly in games for which the Browns are projected to play from behind.

Boston (quadriceps) wasn't present for Friday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealerreports. With Boston now on track to log a trio of 'DNP' listings this week, his status for Sunday night's game against the Raiders is cloudy. Friday's final injury report will reveal whether the Browns' starting WR has any chance to play versus Las Vegas or is ruled out ahead of Week 12 action.

Jeudy recorded two catches on four targets for 74 yards in a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday. Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

Concepcion caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over Houston. He also gained six yards on one carry. Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.

Fannin (groin) was listed as a full practice participant on Thursday's injury report, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. The Browns didn't hold a practice on Thanksgiving Day, but the fact that Fannin was estimated as a full participant Thursday indicates that the second-year tight end is on track to play against the Raiders on Sunday. Fannin has caught at least six passes in three of his last four outings, and has compiled a 25-378-1 receiving line on 32 targets over that span.

availability.comment: Mendoza was 18-for-37 passing for 267 yards, three touchdowns and one interception and had four carries for 22 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss in Denver. After throwing for no touchdowns or interceptions in his first NFL start last Sunday against the Seahawks, Mendoza recorded the first scoring strike of his career on a 68-yard catch and run via RB Ashton Jeanty in Week 11. Mendoza also hooked up with Ian Thomas (19 yards) and Jack Bech (seven yards) for his other two TDs, but he followed up a 58.6 completion percentage in Week 10 with more misfires (19) than connections (18) this Sunday. Mendoza's next chance for game action is next Sunday at Cleveland.

Jeanty's 169 yards from scrimmage amounted to the second-highest single-game total of his career after going for 188 such yards against the Texans in Week 16 of last season. His performance was fueled by a 68-yard catch and run for a touchdown and a 46-yard rush, the latter of which marked his first of 20-plus yards on the campaign. Jeanty also broke a streak of four straight contests falling short of 10 carries, but considering No. 2 RB Mike Washington also earned nine runs in Week 11, the Raiders backfield remains a committee ahead of next Sunday's outing at Cleveland.

The wide receiver appears to have great chemistry with Mendoza, garnering 16 targets over the quarterback's first two career starts.

Mayer missed out on a prime opportunity with top TE Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) inactive in Week 11. Bowers' status will be worth monitoring this week, as an absence from him next Sunday in Cleveland will set up Mayer for another key chance to produce.

availability.comment: Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 35-33 win over Baltimore. The fourth-year QB posted his best single-game completion rate of the season (73.3 percent) while tossing multiple TDs for the third time in the last six contests, a stretch in which he's compiled a 9:5 TD:INT. Both of Young's scores came in the first half, as he connected with Mitchell Evans on a 23-yard TD and Tetairoa McMillan on a seven-yard strike. Young will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against Tampa Bay.

Hrad coach Dave Canales said Monday that Coker has been cleared from the concussion protocol, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports. Coker endured a helmet-to-helmet hit at the end of a six-yard catch in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win against the Ravens, getting shaken up in the process. Afterward, be reportedly entered the concussion protocol, but one day later he doesn't have a head injury. Coker thus is in the clear ahead of next Monday's game at Tampa Bay.

McMillan (foot) was not in uniform for the team stretch portion of Friday's practice, but he did suit up afterward, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported earlier Friday that McMillan was in a helmet and pads, and although he ditched them while stretching he put them back on shortly afterward. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.

Waller (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Friday. Waller was among four Panthers tight ends to have a capped session Friday, the others being Tommy Tremble (knee), Mitchell Evans (Achilles) and Feleipe Franks (wrist). Waller was able to play through his knee injury this past Sunday against the Ravens, when he handled a 46 percent snap share en route to three catches (on three targets) for 42 yards.

Tremble (knee) remained a limited participant at practice Friday. Tremble was limited again Friday after being listed a limited participant on Thursday's practice estimate. He has one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation Saturday, which could help Tremble avoid an injury designation for Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

Mayfield completed 20 of 33 passes for 187 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 36 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Tampa Bay. Mayfield fought through foot and thumb injuries to take the field in a critical game for the 3-6 Buccaneers, but he wasn't able to keep pace with Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs. Mayfield did throw multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season, hitting rookie Ted Hurst for scoring strikes of 23 and four yards. Mayfield's rushing yardage total was also a new season high, and he'll next take aim at the Panthers' beatable secondary in a Week 12 divisional home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 30.

Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards and brought in four of five targets for 43 yards in the Buccaneers 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Gainwell held his usual complementary role on the ground behind a busy Bucky Irving, yet with the Buccaneers trailing throughout the second half, Gainwell was able to finish second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day for Tampa Bay. The veteran back has back-to-back 16-yard efforts on the ground, but Gainwell has a combined 7-103-0 line through the air in that same span heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

Godwin caught three passes for 18 yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions. The veteran wideout ran a team-high 41 routes on Baker Mayfield's 44 dropbacks, but Godwin continues to produce very little with his immense playing time. He's been held under 40 receiving yards in eight straight games and has yet to have a 50-yard receiving game this season. Godwin also has zero touchdowns. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option headed into next Monday night's date with the Panthers.

Egbuka brought in two of five targets for 18 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Egbuka couldn't do much despite tying for the second-most targets on the afternoon for the Buccaneers. The 2025 first-round pick's catch total tied his season low, and he also posted his third sub-20-yard tally of the season. Egbuka has now been held under 50 receiving yards in five consecutive contests heading into a Week 12 Monday night home showdown against the Panthers on Nov. 30.

Hurst caught five of seven targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions. Hurst led the team in targets, and his five catches and 56 receiving yards were new season highs. The wide receiver was able to reach paydirt twice, reeling in a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the second quarter before the pair connected for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. Hurst has now caught 16 of 32 targets for 224 yards and three touchdowns over 10 contests this season.

Johnson did not participate in Friday's practice due to an illness. Johnson wasn't listed on Thursday's practice report, so the illness is a recent development for the second-year wide receiver. His participation level, if any, in Saturday's practice will provide clarity on his status heading into Monday's game against the Panthers.

Otton caught one pass for eight yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions. The tight end earned just a 9.1 percent target share and continues to be nearly invisible in the box score despite being an every-down player who runs virtually every pass route for the Bucs. Otton has just one touchdown since Week 11 of the 2024 season and has just one career 100-yard receiving game across 73 regular-season contests. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet who clearly busts far more than he hits.

Mahomes completed 16 of 29 passes for 174 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed three times for two yards in the Chiefs' 13-10 loss to the Bills on Thursday. He also fumbled twice but recovered on each occasion. Like Josh Allen, Mahomes didn't come close to putting up his typical caliber of production in the poor weather conditions Thursday, although the latter was at least relatively efficient compared to his opposite number. However, Mahomes failed to throw at least one touchdown pass for the first time in five games, and his yardage total was his second-lowest of the campaign. Mahomes will look to bounce back in what will be an appreciably better environment for offense during a Week 13 road matchup against the Rams next Thursday night.

Johnson rushed 17 times for 72 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 24 yards in the Chiefs' 13-10 loss to the Bills on Thursday. Making a third straight start in place of Kenneth Walker (groin), Johnson put together another useful all-around performance that included his third rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run early in the third quarter. Johnson also recorded at least four catches for the third consecutive game, and he's now accumulated 410 scrimmage yards and four total TDs over his three starts. Walker is likely to be back for next Thursday's Week 13 road showdown against the Rams, but Johnson is likely to retain a solid complementary role even when his star teammate is back on the field.

Downs secured one of four targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs' 13-10 loss to the Bills on Thursday. After recording consecutive four-catch tallies following his trade from the Colts, Downs' production saw a downturn Thursday in a game where both air attacks performed below their usual levels. The talented receiver did make good use of his one reception, and Downs should be busier in a Week 13 road matchup against the Rams next Thursday night where weather shouldn't be a factor.

Rice brought in two of five targets for 19 yards in the Chiefs' 13-10 loss to the Bills on Thursday. Rice's production was part of the collateral damage of a night that was unconducive for offense, as the veteran receiver tied his lowest reception and receiving yardage totals of the season for a non-injury-shortened game. Rice came in riding a solid four-game stretch where he'd generated a 23-237-1 line on 27 targets, and he'll look to return to that level of production during a Week 13 road matchup against the Rams next Thursday.

Worthy didn't corral any of his three targets during Thursday's 13-10 loss at Buffalo. Since Josh Downs arrived via trade from Indianapolis at the deadline, Rashee Rice is leading all Chiefs wide receivers in targets with 17 over the last three contests, followed by Downs' 14, Worthy's 10, Cyrus Allen's nine, Jalen Royals' (ankle) two and Andrew Armstrong's two. Worthy's average number of targets has reduced from 5.9 per game pre-Downs to 3.3 since the addition to the position group, and the former has just a 2-38-1 line during that span. As a result, Worthy is difficult to trust as Kansas City prepares to face the Rams on the road next Thursday.

Gray caught all three of his targets for 23 yards during the Chiefs' 13-10 loss to the Bills on Thursday. Gray was cleared to play Thursday after managing a rib injury during Week 12 prep. Patrick Mahomes threw for only 174 yards, and Gray's 23 receiving yards were third most on the Chiefs behind fellow tight end Travis Kelce (71) and rookie running back Emmett Johnson (24). Thursday was the fifth time in 11 regular-season games that Gray caught three passes, and the sixth-year tight end has a 22-234-1 receiving line on 28 targets in 2026.

Kelce brought in four of seven targets for 71 yards in the Chiefs' 13-10 loss to the Bills on Thursday. Kelce, who shook off a hard hit to his lower back late in the first half, ended up posting a game-high receiving yardage total with the help of a game-long 24-yard grab that he made late in the first half, and he also tied for the team lead in receptions. The star tight end did have a couple of missed connections with Patrick Mahomes on fourth-quarter drives, however, plays that could have had an impact on the outcome of such a close game. Kelce has exceeded 65 receiving yards in four of the last five games heading into a Week 13 road showdown against the Rams next Thursday night.

Stafford completed 16 of 23 passes for 141 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed once for no gain in the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers on Wednesday night. He also committed a fumble recovered by Los Angeles. Playing his second game without both Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring), Stafford saw a notable downturn in his numbers and posted a new season low in passing yards. The veteran signal-caller also threw an interception for the fifth straight game, although his pick Wednesday didn't lead to any Packers points since Los Angeles intercepted Jordan Love just two plays later. Stafford also failed to throw a touchdown pass for only the second time this season, and the fact he also lost tight ends Tyler Higbee (chest) and Davis Allen (ankle) to in-game injuries didn't help his cause. On the positive side, there's an outside chance Stafford has Adams back in the fold for a Week 13 home showdown against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3.

Corum rushed 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown and brought in two of three targets for 21 yards in the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers on Wednesday. He also recovered a fumble. Corum's stock had already been trending firmly up in recent weeks, but Wednesday may ultimately go down as the day he formally took the reins of the ground attack from Kyren Williams. The 2024 third-round pick compiled a career-best rushing total while also becoming the first Rams running back to reach the 30-carry threshold in a game during the Sean McVay era that began in 2017. Corum has now logged double-digit carries in five consecutive games, and he capped off his night with productive runs of seven, nine and 29 yards on Los Angeles' game-sealing drive. Corum's fantasy value naturally skyrocketed with Wednesday's performance, and he'll look to build on the outstanding performance in a Week 13 home matchup against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3.

Williams rushed 12 times for 46 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 19 yards in the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers on Wednesday night. Williams had already been losing ground to Blake Corum in recent weeks, but the latter's takeover of the ground attack may have been finalized Wednesday with his career-best 184-yard, one-touchdown effort. Williams logged his final three carries on the Rams' final drive, but Corum was in the clear lead role throughout the majority of the night. Williams did add his seventh rushing touchdown of the campaign on a seven-yard run early in the second quarter, and his backseat role may have been influenced in part by the turf toe injury he's been dealing with for the past month. Nonetheless, Williams could be destined for a true complementary role if McVay opts to center the ground game on Corum moving forward.

Mumpfield brought in four of five targets for 69 yards in the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers on Wednesday night. Mumpfield set the pace in receiving yards for the Rams while also sharing the team lead in both receptions and targets. The 2025 seventh-round pick has now posted back-to-back productive games -- he had a 3-81-0 line in the Week 10 win over the Cardinals -- but Wednesday's performance could have been even more rewarding had an apparent two-yard touchdown grab just before the halfway point of the third quarter not been ruled incomplete on replay. Mumpfield should retain a solid No. 2 role even if Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) returns for a Week 13 home matchup against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3, and the former will retain his No. 1 standing if his star teammate remains sidelined.

Parkinson caught both of his targets for minus-1 yard in a 26-13 victory over the Packers on Wednesday. Parkinson logged a hefty 83 percent offensive snap count, highest among Los Angeles tight ends. His two receptions also tied for the team lead among players at the position, but he couldn't do much with those catches, gaining just one yard on the first and losing two yards on the second. However, Parkinson could take on an even more important role moving forward, as Tyler Higbee (chest) and Davis Allen (ankle) both left Wednesday's win early and didn't return. If neither of those players is ready to suit up in Week 13 against Kansas City on Thursday, Dec. 3, Parkinson and untested rookie Max Klare would lead a tight-end corps that quarterback Matthew Stafford typically looks to often.

Higbee (chest) is considered week-to-week, though it's too early to tell if he may be available Thursday, Dec. 3, against the Chiefs, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports Friday. Higbee and Davis Allen (ankle) were both injured during Wednesday's win over the Packers. Allen likely is facing a multi-week absence due to a high-ankle sprain, but Higbee still has a chance to avoid missing additional action. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare are the only healthy TE options remaining the Rams' active roster.
